$comment: Machine-readable Sprint 6 plan. Prose rationale lives in specs/sprint-6-charter.md; this file is the shape delivery_loop_gate.py consumes. That script is NOT in this repo -- it ships with the pm-skills plugin; resolve it the way specs/sprint-5-loop-plan.json's $comment spells out, with --plan specs/sprint-6-loop-plan.json. Acceptance commands live in scripts/sprint_6_gate.py, one subcommand per task; it reads the sprint, board, epic, ticket keys, room ids and paths from THIS file and holds none of its own. Sprint goal: the office is walkable room to room, and a command proves the bridge carries a real two-turn conversation. Done when (A) the smoke test is green having walked into every room and (B) sprint_6_gate.py live exits 0 with a committed transcript the owner has read. No delivery date -- forecast blackout in force. WIP cap 3; 3 attempts on T2-T6, 2 on T1 and T7; 8 sprint iterations. Reviewers, all advisory: claude-review.yml, GitHub Copilot code review, and the owner's scheduled ChatGPT/Codex PR review, which posts and pushes under the owner's account.
goal: Walkable office + live conversation proof. Done when: (A) godot --headless tests/smoke_test.tscn exits 0 having walked into every room; (B) python3 scripts/sprint_6_gate.py live exits 0 with a committed two-turn transcript from both clients. Sprint 6.

window.note: Jira's required dates, not a delivery forecast

jira.source: docs/delivery-coordinates.md (D-026) owns these; this is the machine-readable copy the gate reads

budgets.note: max_attempts_per_task is the ceiling; a task's own max_attempts may be lower. loop_controller.py spends one iteration per record AND per verify, so eight tasks cost 16 before any retry; 28 is that plus 12 slack and is a different counter from the sprint's 8.

escalation.blocked_on_owner: A PR awaiting the owner's merge is neither a failure nor an attempt. The loop moves to a task whose dependencies are met, otherwise stops and reports.

tasks.title: Fetch and reconcile against origin/dev before any other task runs
tasks.note: Blocking precondition, exempt from the attempt cap. No Jira ticket: it is a precondition the SessionStart hook already runs, and a permanently-instant item would pollute the flow data.

tasks.title: Sprint 6 charter, loop plan and roadmap rewrite
tasks.note: Started 2026-10-06 (PLZG-257 In Progress). Documents this task may touch: the roadmap, the charter, this plan, the doc registry and delivery-coordinates -- nothing else in docs/ or specs/ (risk R5). Done when its PR is merged by the owner and the command exits 0 on dev.

tasks.title: Player's office, engineering floor and war room -- walkable
tasks.note: A room is seen by the probe when a node in group 'rooms' carries a room_id metadata string. The two existing rooms need that too.

tasks.title: Doorway triggers and locked corridors
tasks.note: Doorways: group 'doorways', room_id = the room entered. Locked corridors: group 'locked_corridors', room_id = the room beyond, which GameState.is_unlocked must report false -- the probe drops a corridor whose room is open. No NavigationRegion2D this sprint -- no NPC walks yet, so nothing would consume it.

tasks.title: Smoke test -- every room exists and is reachable (Gate A)
tasks.note: The test moves a body through each doorway in the running scene, bounds read from the scene, never equalities, and prints 'SMOKE rooms_reachable: <ids>' naming what it walked into. It also walks a body at each locked corridor and prints 'SMOKE corridors_blocked: <ids>' for those that stopped it; each id must be one the probe reports as a declared locked corridor. The gate compares the first line with T2's rooms and counts the second against T3's min_locked_corridors, so a test that stops checking a room, or a corridor that is locked in name only, turns the gate red (risk R4).

tasks.title: Live gate -- two real turns through the bridge, in-engine and without Godot (Gate B)
tasks.note: The runner starts bridge/server.py, drives two turns from a headless Godot scene through scenes/bridge/ws_client.gd and the same two from a plain Python websocket client (D-005 swap test, risk R3), and writes the transcript: {captured_at, nonce, owner_read: false, clients: {godot: {turns: [{sent, received} x2]}, python: {...}}}. Turn 1 sends a random nonce; turn 2 asks for it back without repeating it. Up to three tries per run, every try logged (risk R2). The runner exits 2 when it cannot authenticate and the gate passes that through (risk R1). In-engine means the reply reaches BodyLabel through the typewriter. KNOWN BEFORE THE FIRST RUN: bridge/conversation.py's ConversationEngine is stateless -- each request sends only the current task -- so turn 2 cannot recall the nonce and this gate fails until T6 gives the conversation path a history. T5 is done when the runner exists and reports that failure truthfully; its ticket closes on T6's green run, not before.

tasks.title: Fix what the first real Gate B run breaks

known_before_first_run: The conversation path keeps no history between turns (bridge/conversation.py). Counts as defect 1 of 3 when fixed.

tasks.note: Defect 1 is known in advance: the conversation path is stateless, so Gate B's turn 2 cannot pass. How history is carried -- by the client, or by the bridge under a conversation id -- is T6's design call, bounded by D-005: it must work identically for the Godot client and the plain client, and bridge/PROTOCOL.md must describe it. Record each defect fixed as {summary, commit} in acceptance_inputs.defects. A fourth is filed as a ticket and escalated, not absorbed.

tasks.title: Sprint 6 close -- both gates green
tasks.note: Re-runs T1, Gate A and Gate B; requires the transcript committed, captured after the sprint opened (the window's end is Jira's date and is not enforced) and owner_read true (only the owner sets it); requires every other task ticket Done with at least an hour between In Progress and Done; requires a fresh flow snapshot. Starting and closing the Jira sprint are the owner's. Retiring the charter to HISTORICAL follows the Jira close, as PLZG-255 did for Sprint 5.
